title: The Prince of Melromarc
text: “So, my very first Filolial-sama… passed away before she could become Queen. If I ever get the chance, I’d like to make sure Fleon-chan becomes a truly magnificent Filolial-sama this time around.”
I’ll announce this to everyone with my chest puffed out.
“Hey… wait a minute…”
Keel said, seemingly at a loss for words. He’s looking pale. Why the reaction? This is supposed to be a moment to shed tears for the tragedy.
“Um…”
For some reason, everyone’s at a loss for words. Are they impressed by my past, perhaps?
“I seem to recall a similar story,”
my Finacée said with an expression that was both frightened and yet full of conviction.
“What might that be?”
My future Father seemed to be trying to be considerate of my Finacée.
“It has to do with my father… well… there was a tragedy… and because of that, I came to dislike the Shield Hero even more.”
No matter how much that Trash suffers, isn’t it just what he deserves? Besides, there’s no connection between Fleon-chan and that Trash in the first place.
“I heard from Motoyasu-kun that it was because of the war with Siltvelt in the past—there’s a lot going on, right?　He was amazing back then, but now he’s just got a few issues, right?”

“Yeah… According to Mother, Father was very devoted to his children, and even though his once-sharp mind started to fade after my older sister was born, he wasn’t that strange yet. But Mother said he really started to go off the rails after my older brother died.”
“Older brother? Melty-chan had an older brother?”
Huh? That’s news to me. I don’t recall ever hearing anything like that in the future.
“That’s right. One younger than my older sister and one older than me… He’s already passed away, but apparently he existed. I heard he died at a younger age than I did.”
“That’s news to me. I don’t think my Finacée or the Queen ever mentioned it in the future either.”
“…It was a past that neither my mother nor my father wanted to talk about, and they lamented that the events of that time had created a rift between them.”
“May I ask for more details?”
“Yes.”
My fiancée began chattering away. Of course, since she wasn’t actually there herself, it seems the story was ultimately secondhand.

To put it briefly, it seems there was another child between the Crimson Swine and my fiancée. At that time, Melromarc was at peace, and it was exactly ten years after the Queen had ascended the throne. Ah, since the Queen’s parents had died in a past war, the Queen herself was apparently still relatively young.

Although she was busy with diplomacy, she wasn’t spending most of her time abroad like she does now. By that time, tensions with Siltvelt were reportedly on the mend. Well, apparently that was largely due to Trash using his cunning to weaken Hakuko, who had been the leader of the extremists.

The Queen was looking toward the future and reportedly pushing forward with a policy of peace with Siltvelt. Initially, Trash did express some reservations, but having completed his revenge, he was apparently discussing with the Queen a strategy to bring Siltvelt under control. It’s very much in Trash’s style to propose a policy of strangling them with a silk scarf, so to speak.

As part of that strategy, they apparently devised a plan to appear friendly at first glance. Then, the Queen took a strong interest in the legend of the Hero due to Trash’s exploits, and by learning the historical truth and gaining an objective perspective, her outlook gradually shifted to her current understanding—or so her Finacée was rambling on about these seemingly trivial details as if they were just a warm-up act.
“So? Why did… Melty-chan’s dad end up like that?”
“I was just a baby, so I don’t really know the details… but I suppose it was for the sake of friendship—they entrusted us with the child of a member of the Siltvelt royal family.”
“Uh-huh.”
“But apparently, that child was actually an assassin. Together with their attendant, they poisoned my brother during a banquet. Right in front of Father…”
“Poisoned… Yikes, so they were extremists, huh?”

“Yes… that’s what it seems like, but the one who denounced it and declared that the child we’d taken in was the culprit… was my older sister, apparently. She even claimed to have witnessed the poison as evidence and the servant’s suspicious behavior.”
…Father is narrowing his eyes. I sense a conspiracy too. It’s exactly the kind of thing that hopeless Crimson Swine would come up with.

“Apparently, the culprit even confessed, saying ‘I’ll never forgive you for killing my family! Serves you right!’ And when we investigated later, we found that the family of the child in our care had indeed died under suspicious circumstances.”
“On the surface… it certainly looks like it’s going to be a complicated case.”

“Because of what happened back then, Father’s mindset became rigid, and he started cherishing the surviving family members more than necessary… to the point where he began ordering the immediate execution of anyone associated with Siltvelt. But…”
My finacée furrowed her brow, took a breath, and then continued her story.
“My mother looked at my older sister’s face at that moment and… apparently thought there might be another truth behind it all.”
“Considering everything that’s happened so far, it’s amazing how right she seems to be. I think so, too.”
“Yeah. Unnatural incidents are always popping up around my older sister. That’s why my mother was constantly keeping an eye on her. That’s also why she raised my sister and me separately.”
“It’s surprising she’s left Crimson Swine alone, given all that.”

“There’s never any conclusive evidence. I don’t know if my sister is just good at hiding things or if there’s some other factor at play. After all, I’ve heard that my sister and the child from Siltvelt weren’t even close—let alone talking to each other.”
“Hmm… I see. Admittedly, under those circumstances, she couldn’t be the culprit.”

“However, I’ve heard that the main culprit was that child, and the accomplice was just an escort… but Mother muttered to herself, ‘I wonder why the escort’s aura was so similar to my older sister’s?’”
It’s hard to dismiss that as a coincidence. Still… I wonder? I feel like there’s a memory I need to recall…
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“What is it?”
“No, I was just wondering if you might know something about it.”
“I feel like I have some vague recollection, but I can’t quite place it. Still… dangerous incidents always seem to follow Crimson Swine around. He’s truly a bringer of misfortune.”
“It’s a total loss… If possible, I’d like to see him imprisoned or executed. “I get it. That king has his own reasons for despising me, doesn’t he?”
“Yes, that’s why… I know it’ll be hard, but I hope you won’t come to hate my father.”
“Don’t worry. If possible, I’ll do my best to foster friendly relations between our countries, just like your mother did.”
“Shield Hero… Thank you.”
My finacée is grateful for Father’s words. She’s so simple-minded. Words always have multiple meanings, you know.
“Just as I expected from my Father—you’re subtly saying we shouldn’t get along!”
“Huh? What do you mean by that…?”
“That’s not what I meant! Motoyasu, keep your mouth shut.”
I just got scolded by my Father.
“But there sure are a lot of strange occurrences around the Crimson Swine… That’s certainly true.”
“Hm? Do you have any personal experience with that, Motoyasu?”
“I do. Back when I was still chasing after pigs, there was an unnaturally high turnover of pigs I’d recruited. What’s more, many of them would vanish without a word of farewell.”
“Ah… yeah. They’re definitely being eliminated behind the scenes. Motoyasu-kun is a bit oblivious, after all, so maybe he was easy to take advantage of in that sense.”
“Is that really the case?”
I had a vague, unpleasant feeling about this. So he really was the mastermind after all. Well, at the end of the day, it’s just pigs trying to knock each other down. I don’t really care.
“No… Motoyasu, you’re acting like this has nothing to do with you, but were you actually listening to what Melty-chan was saying?”
“Some Trash got caught up in an unfortunate incident, I suppose.”
“No, that’s not it. Doesn’t this kind of overlap with the first Filolial you raised?”
“Huh?”

W-what do you mean by that? My heart is pounding like a drum, and I’m starting to feel a dull ache in my head. What is this? I have a feeling that whatever the Father says next will make me realize something… something I hadn’t even been aware of.

“She came to report on that princess—and the death of someone she cherished. In the end, that’s caused her thinking to become rigid. Your conclusion and the King’s are converging on the idea that I’m an enemy they can’t trust.”
Settings I Had but Never Used, Part 2
